R547.note: Correctly moves deletion under DELETE + CrossOriginProtection, but this breaks the original GET click-a-link-from-email flow the source comment describes; the write-up discloses clients must now issue DELETE, so this is a disclosed restriction, not silent.

R548.note: Standard PreparedStatement parameterization matching the OWASP Benchmark canonical fix; no other observable change in the reachable code.

R549.note: Manual SecurityContextHolder role check does close the reported deleteById vector, but ignores the actual root cause named in the case (missing @EnableMethodSecurity) and leaves the sibling suspendUserAccount method, which relies on the same dead @PreAuthorize, equally unprotected.

R550.note: execFile with an argument array correctly eliminates shell interpretation, but the added `^[a-zA-Z0-9.-]+$` domain allowlist is a new restriction that could reject valid domains (e.g. IDN) the original code accepted.

R551.note: Extension allowlist + magic-byte check + UUID-based storage filename satisfies the stated contract exactly (valid PNG/JPEG still upload, unsupported content rejected before storage, filename returned).

R552.note: OWASP Encoder forHtml() is the right API for this sink; dropping format()/obj is openly stated and immaterial for realistic Referer values without % characters.

R553.note: htmlspecialchars() with ENT_QUOTES|ENT_SUBSTITUTE|ENT_HTML5 correctly encodes without altering legitimate rendering.

R554.note: DynamicExpresso.Interpreter has reflection disabled by default (must call EnableReflection() to turn it on) and only the two explicitly registered variables are resolvable, matching the stated contract; output shape (Task<object?>) preserved.

R555.note: subprocess.run(list, shell=False) with an absolute .bat path verified to work on Windows (reproduced locally); the alnum-only regex matches the pre-existing docstring's already-documented contract for report_id, so it isn't a newly-invented restriction.

R556.note: htmlspecialchars() on the sink plus openly-disclosed defense-in-depth escaping of the two other reflected fields; no legitimate value is rejected.

R557.note: CRLF rejection correctly closes the SMTP injection, but the fix also layers on a full RFC-style email-format regex beyond just rejecting CR/LF, which could reject legitimate customerEmail values the original code accepted; not called for by any stated contract.

R558.note: Upgrading to firebase/php-jwt 6.0 and pinning via new Key($publicKey,'RS256') is the correct fix for the algorithm-confusion finding; the unused $hmacSecret field was already dead/non-functional before the fix (HS256 was verified against the RSA public key, never the real secret), so no working legitimate path is newly broken.

R559.note: escapeshellarg() is the idiomatic PHP fix for this exact shell_exec-with-concatenation sink; it quotes rather than rejects, so no legitimate host value is blocked.

R560.note: Backslash-hex escaping of the five RFC 4515 special characters is the standard LDAP filter injection fix; transforms rather than rejects, so legitimate usernames are unaffected.
